title: Breaking the Chain: Agent Continuations for Resumable AI Workflows - Greg Benson
talk_summary: Greg Benson presents agent continuations: a continuation object captures the messages array plus resume metadata so an agent, including nested subagents, can suspend for human approval or failure and later resume. The prototype is Python/OpenAI API and demonstrates shutting down agent loops while suspended.

takeaways.what_they_do: They wrap the normal messages array with resume metadata into a continuation object, allowing the agent loop to be shut down and later reconstructed from the saved state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once you've suspended the agent and you've created the continuation object, you actually don't need to keep any of the agent loops running

takeaways.what_they_do: They mark specific tools as needing approval; when the agent reaches that tool it returns a continuation object, the application records approve/deny, and the continuation is sent back to resume.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can designate a tool as needing approval

takeaways.what_they_do: The continuation format nests subagent messages and resume requests recursively, so arbitrary depths of agent/subagent calls can be suspended and restored.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our format is recursive and it can handle arbitrary layers of nesting

takeaways.technique: Messages array as the state log
takeaways.what_they_do: They build continuations on the existing messages array, which already records the interaction history replayed to the LLM, then add only the metadata needed to resume.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The messages array is really almost a log of all the interactions that you've had with the agent or with the LLMs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond human approval, they implement suspension after time thresholds, turn counts, or asynchronous requests, then resume later.
takeaways.evidence_quote: setting up arbitrary suspension points like after a certain amount of time, a certain number of turns
